title: Walmart shares delivery update consumers need to know about
detail:
Walmart shares delivery update consumers need to know about
Maurie Backman
Sat, November 21, 2026 at 11:17 AM CST 3 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart has become an increasingly important destination for consumers looking to save money on groceries and everyday essentials. 

But low prices aren't the only reason shoppers keep returning to the retailer. Convenience is becoming just as important.

As more consumers turn to online shopping, Walmart is making significant investments in its delivery network, using its thousands of physical stores to get products into customers' hands faster.

The strategy is already producing results, and the company recently shared an update that could have major implications for how Americans shop.

Walmart expands delivery reach using its stores

During the company's third quarter 2027 earnings call, Walmart CEO John Furner discussed how the retailer's expanding delivery capabilities are helping connect its stores and digital operations.

"We no longer see stores and e-commerce as separate, but connected parts of an integrated ecosystem," Furner told analysts.

Furner also said, "We can now reach 96% of U.S. households in less than three hours, and 60% in less than 30 minutes. We have a unique ability to get closer to customers, use inventory more effectively, and deliver with speed at a low relative cost."

The comments highlight an important shift in Walmart's business model. 

Rather than treating online shopping and traditional store visits as competing channels, the retailer is increasingly using them together to improve convenience and attract more customers.

For shoppers, that could mean faster deliveries, more available products, and fewer reasons to shop elsewhere.

The company is also making more products available for local delivery by placing select marketplace inventory in stores. That means customers can access a broader assortment without necessarily waiting for products to arrive from distant fulfillment centers.

Walmart is also expanding beyond traditional retail orders. Furner said the company is using its delivery capabilities to support quick-service restaurant partners, allowing customers to order food alongside other essentials.

Iv-olga/Shutterstock.com
Walmart's loyal customers keep coming back

Walmart's delivery expansion also comes as the retailer benefits from consistent customer traffic.

A Placer.ai report examined foot traffic and shopping frequency at Walmart and Target during the third quarter of 2026. It found that Walmart's overall visits increased 0.7% year over year, while same-store visits rose 0.6%.

Perhaps more importantly, 67.7% of Walmart visitors came to the retailer at least twice during an average month, suggesting Walmart has maintained a remarkably consistent base of repeat shoppers.

Walmart CFO Expects "the Next 5 Years to Look Better Than the Last 5 Years." At Its Premium Multiple, It Has To ©@Изображения пользователя Anton Estrada via Canva, @PixelsEffect from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Walmart beat and raised its outlook again on Nov. 19, but the stock fell anyway at 42x forward earnings.

CFO John David Rainey expects the next five years to beat the last five.

Its operating margin slipped from 4.5% to 4.2% over five fiscal years, yet analysts expect about 11% EPS growth a year.

At that multiple, investors are paying for a wider margin.

Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) beat estimates and raised its full-year outlook for the second straight quarter on Nov. 19. The stock fell anyway.

The price helps explain why. At 42x forward earnings, Walmart trades well above Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) at 25x and Target (TGT:NYSE) at 17x. Only Costco (COST:NASDAQ) trades richer, at about 49x.

On the call, UBS's Michael Lasser asked whether Walmart could sustain its "algorithm" of 4% sales growth and up to 8% operating income growth next year. CFO John David Rainey said operating income would keep growing faster than sales next year, then went further: "we expect the next five years to look better than the last five years."

At 42x, it has to.

Analysts Already Expect a Much Better Five Years

Over the last five fiscal years, Walmart's normalized EPS grew about 5% a year. Analysts expect roughly twice that pace from here, about 11% a year, to $3.62 in the year ending January 2029:

WMT Normalized EPS, Actual and Consensus Estimates: FY2024-FY2029 (TIKR)

At about 4% sales growth, getting there would take a wider margin, with some help from buybacks. Instead, its operating margin slipped from 4.5% to 4.2% over those five years:

WMT Operating Margin: FY2022-FY2026 (TIKR)
Investors Are Already Paying for Walmart's Better Five Years

That 42x is below February's peak of 47x but well above Walmart's five-year average of 30x:

WMT Stock NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)

If it drifted back to that average, earnings would need to rise about 40% to hold the share price, or a bit over three years at 11% a year.

E-Commerce Is Close to Paying Its Own Way

Rainey's case rests on e-commerce, which earned a U.S. incremental margin above 12% in the quarter. He said U.S. e-commerce is "pretty close to breakeven without advertising, which was pretty remarkable." He expects low double-digit incremental margins from here.

E-commerce is about 25% of Walmart's business, and Rainey sees that share rising another 10 to 15 percentage points over five to seven years. If it pays its own way, more of each ad dollar and membership fee falls through to profit.

Amazon's North America segment shows where that can lead: an operating margin of about 7% in 2025, against 5.2% for the Walmart U.S. segment in the year ended January 2026.

title: Why Isn't Walmart's Stock Bouncing Back After Weak Earnings Results?
detail:
Why Isn't Walmart's Stock Bouncing Back After Weak Earnings Results?
Eric Volkman, The Motley Fool
Sat, November 21, 2026 at 7:57 AM CST 5 min read
WMT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart's (NASDAQ:WMT) third-quarter results, which were posted Thursday morning, certainly weren't bad. The massive retailer topped analyst estimates, if only slightly, and delivered growth in both revenue and non-GAAP, or adjusted, earnings per share (EPS).

But the company's growth rates for key metrics were lower than in the second quarter, including two that had soared in previous frames. I think this is why Walmart's stock slumped during Thursday's trading session, only to recover the following day amid investor rotation out of beleaguered tech stocks and into defensive sectors like retail.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Two thin beats

To put some concrete numbers and percentages on this, Walmart's third-quarter revenue totaled $188.8 billion, which was 5.2% higher year over year. This was on the back of comparable sales in its core Walmart U.S. operations that rose by 2.9% when stripping out fuel sales. On a constant-currency basis, revenue was 4.5% higher at $187.6 billion.

On the bottom line, attributable net income under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) sank in that one-year stretch, falling to just under $4.95 billion from the year-ago $6.14 billion. Yet on the non-GAAP (adjusted), per-share basis that analysts and many investors consider a truer indication of profitability, there was an improvement. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.65 from third quarter 2026's $0.62 for a 4.8% increase.

Those leading fundamentals were barely high enough to outpace the consensus analyst estimates of almost $187.3 billion for headline revenue and $0.64 per share for adjusted net profit.

CEO John Furner flagged the quarter as a resounding success. This, he was quoted as saying, derived from "growing our core business and gaining market share. The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more."

That growth, however, was down from the second quarter's headline revenue increase of 5.9% and the 19% rise in adjusted EPS to $0.81. At least frame No. 3's 2.9% bump in U.S. Walmart ex-fuel "comps" (modestly) topped the previous quarter's 2.6%.

Another major growth driver, global e-commerce sales, advanced 17% year over year. This sounds very robust until it's compared to the second quarter's 23%. A smaller but fast-emerging revenue stream, the company's global advertising business, slowed to 25% year over year from the quarter-ago gain of 38%.

Walmart shoppers were stocking up on numerous emergency supplies after a series of technology outages that disrupted day-to-day activities and alarmed Americans across the country.

Shoppers loaded their carts with propane, bottled water and camping gear, a Walmart spokesperson told Reuters.

"We have seen a small amount of that. Certainly, categories like jug bottled water or propane are selling at higher comps with that concern, but it's really relatively small to our overall business. It's worth noting that oftentimes when we see that, it's a pull forward of future demand," Walmart Chief Financial Officer John David Rainey told Yahoo Finance.

The retailer also raised its annual sales and profit forecasts on Thursday, anticipating growth in its delivery and membership as it prepares for the holiday shopping season.

Costco Sees Panic Buying Surge After Tech Outages, Report Says

Walmart shoppers were stocking up on numerous emergency supplies after a series of technology outages.

Walmart is the largest retailer to report the uptick in emergency supply purchases, but other companies said they experienced similar sales in response to the outages.

Read On The Fox Business App

Costco and Tractor Supply are among the other retailers to see an increase in demand amid a wave of apparent panic buying.

Mizuho Securities analyst David Bellinger said the string of technology disruptions led to a sudden surge in emergency preparedness shopping at Costco.

About 21 of the 26 high-ticket generators Costco offers on its website were sold out as of Sunday night, according to a note released by Mizuho Securities on Monday.

Among the wiped-out inventory were massive whole-home backup systems priced as high as nearly $7,000.

Walmart shoppers stocked up on propane, bottled water and camping gear.

"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at [Costco]," Bellinger said in the note.

The buying spree has helped put Costco on pace for rare double-digit U.S. sales growth this month, marking a level not seen since mid-2022.

Shoppers are also aggressively "pantry-loading" on bulk essentials ahead of the holiday season, the report said.

Walmart Raises Full-year Outlook As Wealthier Shoppers Fuel Sales Growth

Costco and Tractor Supply are among the other retailers to see an increase in demand for emergency supplies.

Bellinger raised his price target on Costco shares from $1,100 to $1,150 on the back of the heightened demand.

Meanwhile, Tractor Supply told Bloomberg News sales of products like generators, liquid storage tanks and propane accessories are trending higher this year. For the first time, shoppers are buying these products at a higher rate than across other product groups.

Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) grew into a popular shopping destination due to its ultra-low prices. Along with technology investments that have kept the company competitive with the likes of Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), it has regularly posted gains in sales and earnings over the years.

And it's still growing. In its most recent fiscal quarter -- fiscal 2026 Q3, which ended on Oct. 31. -- its adjusted revenue grew 4.5% year over year, helping drive a 4.8% increase in adjusted earnings per share.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

In addition to investing for growth, Walmart rewards its shareholders with dividends. In fact, management has raised the payout for 53 straight years. That makes it a Dividend King, a title only earned by those rare companies with payout-hiking streaks of at least 50 consecutive years.

Image source: Getty Images.

In February, the board of directors raised the quarterly payout from $0.235 per share to $0.2475 per share. With a payout ratio (dividends divided by earnings) of 37%, Walmart can easily afford that payment.

If you decided to invest just over $10,000 in Walmart's stock, you could purchase 78 shares. That would provide annual dividend income of about $77.

However, investors should note the less-than-average dividend yield. At the current share price, Walmart stock yields 0.8% compared to 1.1% for the average stock in the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC).

Walmart's stock also looks expensive right now based on historical valuation and compared to the S&P 500. It trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 47, up from 40 at the start of the year. That's much higher than Walmart's 10-year median P/E of 32. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 currently has a P/E multiple of 24.

There's no doubt that Walmart is one of the world's most successful retailers, and it retains its competitive advantages by offering hard-to-beat prices. But its relatively low dividend yield and rich valuation mean I'd stay away from Walmart's stock right now.

NasdaqGS:WMT Trailing 12-Month Earnings & Revenue History as at Nov 2026
Walmart's higher margin mix: promise vs delivery

Bulls in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St argue that profits should tilt toward richer fee pools over time.

"The main factor that has to go right is the continued growth and profitability of higher margin alternative profit pools such as advertising, marketplace services, and membership, alongside investment in automation and ultra fast fulfillment."

Q3 shows progress toward that target. U.S. advertising grew 37%, marketplace and fulfillment services net sales climbed 49%, and membership fee revenue rose 17%. Global e commerce advanced 17% with U.S. e commerce up 23%, and management flagged low double digit incremental margins here. Those shifts help offset softer net income and EPS in the quarter.

Walmart risk check: growth engines vs profit drag

The same Narrative warns that digital expansion could weigh on group earnings power.

"While Walmart's e-commerce and digital businesses are growing rapidly, international e-commerce operations are still described as loss making and delivery and logistics costs on grocery continue to pressure net margins."

Reported Q3 numbers cut against a broad margin squeeze story. Adjusted operating income increased 5.5% on 4.4% sales growth, and management lifted full year operating income guidance to a range of 8% to 8.6%. E commerce excluding advertising is described as nearing breakeven, with low double digit incremental margins. That suggests efficiency gains and a richer fee mix are, for now, outrunning the drag from loss making pockets.

Walmart WMT shares were down after Thursday's Q3 results, but they were among the few to be in the green on Friday in a broadly down day for the market. Unlike Target TGT, which had come out with truly impressive results Wednesday morning, Walmart's results were ok; not great, but not bad either.

As we noted about Walmart shares recently, their defensive attributes position them to stand their ground during periods of market turmoil. Market participants are clearly grappling with some weighty questions about the broader AI space, with even the long-awaited Anthropic ANT stock losing ground the day after its successful debut.

Walmart shares' recent struggles notwithstanding, they have outperformed peers like Target TGT and even Amazon AMZN over the last five years, up more than +184.2% vs. +38.5% for Amazon and -19.4% for Target. Walmart's +184.2% gain over the last five years compares to a +69.2% gain for the S&P 500 index.

Unlike this standout performance over the last five years, Walmart shares seem to have lost their mojo this year, even though they appear to be rebounding lately, as the year-to-date performance chart below for Walmart, Target, Amazon, and the S&P 500 index shows.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Walmart shares fell sharply after the last quarterly release on August 20th, reflecting a combination of factors, including a seemingly lower-quality earnings beat (benefiting from tariff refunds), decelerating comp growth, and underwhelming Q3 guidance.

Walmart and other big-box retailers are undoubtedly facing a difficult operating environment, with elevated fuel costs not only adding to consumers' financial burdens but also increasing retailers' expenses. Walmart noted on the Q3 earnings call that elevated diesel and transportation costs have added $2 billion to their cost base this year.

A big worry among Walmart investors is decelerating same-store sales or comp growth, which came in at +2.9% for Q3 vs. +2.6% in Q2 and +4.1% in Q1. Comps were north of +4% in each of the preceding year's quarters.

Target appears to have firmly put its struggles of the last couple of years behind it, with Q3 comps coming in at +5.6% (vs. estimates of +3.07%). This was the third quarter in a row that Target posted better-than-expected comps.

It is important to keep in mind that Walmart shares command a premium valuation, trading at 40X forward 12-month EPS estimates, only modestly below the 10-year high of 45.4X in February 2026.
